title: Dad's Tomato Sauce
description: David’s large batch tomato sauce with a long stovetop simmer, Parmesan in two additions, optional red wine, and a final slow reduction in a 275°F / 135°C oven.
cookTime: 2–3 hours on the stove, then oven reduction until 2.5–5 cm lower
totalTime: Several hours, depending on the oven reduction
yield: Large batch; portion into jars and freeze
ingredients: 8,165 g tomatoes, whole, diced, crushed, or a mix (18 lb)
300 g Parmesan cheese, divided into 100 g and 200 g additions
About 236 mL red wine (about 235 g), optional
Salt, oregano, basil, black pepper, garlic powder, parsley, onion powder, crushed red pepper, and Italian seasoning blend, to taste
steps: Roughly chop the onion, carrot, and celery while the olive oil heats in a large oven safe pot.
Add the onion, carrot, and celery. Sauté until soft without browning. Add the diced garlic for the final minute and season lightly with salt.
Add the tomato paste and cook with the vegetables for 1–3 minutes.
Add all the tomatoes, stir well, and salt generously.

Add 100 g of the Parmesan and the dried seasonings to taste. The handwritten guide is about 1½ tablespoons of each spice, with the blend adjusted by taste. Blend the sauce with a stick blender to the texture you like.
Add the bay leaves. Simmer on the stovetop for another 2–3 hours, stirring occasionally.
Heat the oven to 275°F / 135°C. Add the remaining 200 g Parmesan and, if using, about 236 mL red wine. Stir and simmer a little longer, then taste and adjust the seasonings.
Partially cover the pot and transfer it to the oven. Stir every 45–60 minutes. Let the sauce darken and reduce until its level falls about 2.5–5 cm (1–2 inches).
Remove the bay leaves, taste and adjust the seasonings again. Let cool, portion into jars, and freeze.
notes: This replaces the earlier reconstruction with David's handwritten method. The tomato quantity is 18 lb / 8.165 kg and the tomato paste is 2 lb / 0.91 kg. Wine may be omitted or added at any point from the tomato addition through the final stovetop stage. The original gives seasonings by taste and suggests roughly 1½ tablespoons of each spice, so exact gram weights would imply precision the recipe does not have. Keep the two Parmesan additions and the 2–3 hour stovetop simmer before the oven reduction.
